name: skill_state_transition
description: TypeScript-only (not yet ported to AxIR; see the backlog entry). Core-owned skillState transition semantics: the real SHA-256 rationale digest over canonical bytes, the compare-and-set revision advance, the kernel's BOUNDED single rebase, the mapping of a persistently lost write onto rejection 'fence', and the rule that only an ACCEPTED transition enters the ledger. Host-supplied checker behaviour is deliberately NOT expected here; the checker declared below is a no-op. The store the runner supplies is seeded at revision 4 (a run that has already committed) and, for the second writer only, models a competing writer that commits immediately after each read — the only way a single bounded rebase can still lose. Both are behaviours the declared AxProgramStateStore contract permits; what is asserted is what the kernel does when the store behaves that way.

skill.name: Warehouse picking procedure
skill.content: Pick every line on the order, then close the goal by citing the newest inventory.pick receipt ref from the Receipt Roster.

expected.storedRevisionAfterNote: The loser's committedRevision is 5, not 6: it rebased onto revision 5 and then lost again, so it never committed and reports the revision it last read. The store reaches 7 because the competing writer commits after each of the loser's two reads — one for the rebase, one for the conflict-versus-outage check.
